items.finding: The source reports that temperature was varied together with acid concentrations and ionic strength to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: For O2, this suggests treating product temperature as a calibration variable and testing whether an in-line temperature reading improves the composition assessment.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work concerns reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not an in-line temperature sensor in opaque concentrated milk; the benefit of temperature logging would need to be tested on this product and line.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E01 ¶19

items.finding: The source notes that contamination of the probe window can make an accurate measurement impossible in a process where a binder is added.
items.how_it_applies: For O2, this supports including a probe-window fouling and cleaning check in the practical comparison, for example by comparing signal before and after cleaning.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a pharmaceutical process with a binder, not an opaque concentrated milk product; the fouling mechanism, rate and cleanability may differ.

citation.quote: However, an accurate measurement may not be possible because of contamination of the probe window due to the addition of a binder during the process, which is a disadvantage.
citation.label: E02 ¶27

items.finding: The source states that NIRS signals are harder to interpret than conventional analysis methods because overlapping absorption bands make the spectra complex.
items.how_it_applies: For O1, this suggests planning spectral interpretation support and retaining reference analyses in the comparison experiment to check whether fat and protein changes are distinguishable.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general NIRS limitation, not a result for this opaque concentrated milk product or a specific instrument; spectral complexity and interpretability would need to be tested here.

citation.quote: However, a disadvantage of NIRS is that it is more difficult to interpret a signal than by using conventional analysis methods, such as chromatography, ultraviolet/visible (UV-VIS) light, and others, because the absorption bands overlap due to spectral complexity.
citation.label: E02 ¶13
